title: Execution-path sieve: adaptive operator-mapper & autotune for seq-len x architecture
creator: Jun Park
description:
Goal: Build an execution-path sieve (EPS) that adaptively maps high-level operator choices (attention kernels, matmul variants, tiled ops) to concrete implementations based on two axes: sequence-length distribution for the request, and hardware architecture fingerprint (GPU family, SMs, memory bandwidth). The EPS should: 1) produce near-optimal latency/cost for common traffic slices; 2) gracefully fallback to conservative kernels under tight SLOs; 3) warm-start from small profiling probes and continually refine choices with lightweight online metrics.

Background: Current kernel selector uses static heuristics and a small offline table. That leads to suboptimal choices when sequence length distributions shift (e.g., prefill-heavy workloads vs. single-token decode) or when running on new GPU families with different memory/compute balance. Several recent incidents showed latency regressions for 2-8K prefill requests on Ampere-analog instances.

Proposal: Implement EPS composed of three components: (1) Fast fingerprinting layer that extracts seqlen-bucket and architecture-bucket from each incoming request and node; (2) Lightweight probe scheduler that occasionally runs microbenchmarks at low traffic to calibrate kernel cost estimates for the current binary/kernels; (3) Bayesian policy layer that picks a kernel variant for prefill and decode separately with regret-bounded exploration. The policy uses a cost model combining p99 latency, throughput impact (tokens/sec), and GPU occupancy estimate.

Key design choices and trade-offs: - Prefill vs decode decoupling: treat prefill and decode as separate decision points because their memory/compute profiles differ significantly. Implementation will maintain separate profile tables and probe budgets. - Probe budget: probes must be rare and low-impact. Default probe budget will be 0.1% of traffic per seqlen-bucket with exponential backoff on errors. - Storage: profile table stored on local node with periodic async aggregation to the control plane for cross-node smoothing. To avoid large metadata, we use compact fingerprints (4-6 bytes) per kernel variant. - Safety: include SLO-guard rails that prevent switching to higher variance kernels if recent p99 exceeds threshold or error rates increase. Switches are canaried across a small subset of requests before wide rollout.

Metrics: Primary metrics are request p99 latency, median token cost, and throughput (tokens/sec) at cluster-level. Secondary metrics: probe-induced tail spikes, kernel switch churn, accuracy of predicted cost delta. Success targets: reduce p99 by >=10% for prefill-heavy workloads and reduce token cost by >=6% for mixed workloads without increasing error rates.

Rollout plan: implement in two stages: local node-only EPS with no cross-node aggregation (can be toggled per deployment) -> gradual enabling of cross-node aggregation and control-plane suggested kernel maps -> A/B rollout across a subset of customers on runtime-1.20.

Compatibility: Works with existing batching and KV cache behavior. Will add hooks so batching layer can request kernel hints (e.g., small-batch-optimized kernel) from EPS. EPS must respect existing model pins and forced kernel overrides in Dedicated and Private deployments.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Marco Delgado: Spike completed. Microprobe harness shows clear perf ordering on T4 vs A100 for 1-64 vs >1024 seqlen. Data uploaded to Benchmark dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/bench/eps-spike-2025-01-12

2025-01-20 - Aisha Raman: Implemented fingerprint layer prototype. Fingerprint includes GPU family enum, sm_count bucket, mem_bw_estimate, and seqlen_bucket (0-8,9-64,65-512,513-4096,4097+). Initial memory cost ~220 bytes per model entry.

2025-01-28 - Jun Park (PM): Reviewed probe budget proposal. Concern: 0.1% might be noisy for low-traffic customers; propose floor and cap per-customer. Added to dependencies -> ENG-45678 (customer-level probe policy).
2025-01-30 - SRE - L. Chen: Observability hooks added for probe traces; ensure probes emit span tags: eps.probe=true, kernel.variant, seqlen_bucket, probe_latency_ms.

2025-02-03 - Aisha Raman: Bayesian policy v1 merged to feature branch (github PR below). Local node-only mode is functional; did not enable cross-node aggregation. Running cluster perf tests on runtime-1.19-beta.

2025-02-05 - Performance team: Perf run summary: prefill p99 improved 12% for 2-8k seqlen bin on Ampere; token cost reduced 4% across mixed workload. Probe overhead ~0.03% additional tokens. Planning follow-up tuning to hit token cost target.
acceptance_criteria: EPS can select different kernels for prefill vs decode on a per-request basis.
Perf regression guard rails block unsafe kernel switches and emit alerts.
Probe budget configurable at customer and cluster level; default safeguards in place.
Automated perf test shows >=10% p99 improvement in at least two seqlen buckets in our perf lab before rollout.
Documentation and ops-runbook created for toggling EPS and inspecting profile tables.
steps: Implement fingerprinting + seqlen buckets in request preprocessor
Integrate microprobe harness and probe scheduler into runtime
Build Bayesian policy layer and local profile table storage
Add safety and SLO guard rails + canary switch path
Add aggregation pipeline to control plane (phase 2)
Roll out node-only EPS to staging -> runtime-1.19-beta test -> runtime-1.20 canary customers
